chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Sadan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever dies without performing the Hajj of Islam, and nothing prevented him from doing so except a burdensome need, or an illness that makes him unable to perform Hajj because of it, or a ruler who prevents him, then let him die a Jew or a Christian.'

key_terms.مَرَضٌ لَا يُطِيقُ الْحَجَّ: An illness that prevents performing Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who dies without performing Hajj if they had no valid excuse?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-Amal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) emphasis on the urgency of Hajj, noting that the phrase 'let him die a Jew or a Christian' serves as a metaphor for the gravity of neglecting this pillar when capable, rather than a literal change in creed. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that valid excuses must be genuine impediments (like severe illness or debt), and mere laziness or preference does not exempt one from this fundamental duty of Islam.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  It is narrated that Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “One who dies before performing an obligatory Hajj without having a valid reason, like illness or rule of an oppressive king, he has an option either to die as a Jew or a Christian.”
